items.title: Alan Jones told 17yo 'there are no rules' at his home, court hears
items.description: A man accusing Alan Jones of indecently assaulting him has detailed in court a night at the broadcaster's farm, where he said Mr Jones demanded he have a shower and come out wearing "a robe and nothing else".

items.title: Questions about Sydney protest spark tense exchange at royal commission
items.description: The head of a peak Jewish body has criticised the conduct of protesters at a pro-Palestinian rally in the wake of Hamas's attack on Israel, prompting a tense exchange at the antisemitism royal commission.

items.title: Billion-dollar property collapse highlights private credit danger
items.description: Examinations of the downfall of Jon Adgemis's property empire may well shed light on the extent to which private credit firms, essentially a shadow banking industry with little or no regulation, have their hooks into the economy.

items.title: 'Not on your life': Ex-NSW minister quizzed over friend's donation
items.description: Damien Tudehope tells the state's corruption inquiry he did not believe payments made by  his friend and hotelier Michael O'Hara, a prohibited donor, were political donations.

items.title: Inside 'Kraken's' sting that led to Sydney underworld figure's arrest
items.description: Sam Amine is awaiting sentence in the NSW District Court after pleading guilty to brokering the supply of the drugs and firearm.

items.title: US vow to dismantle the International Criminal Court labelled 'very worrying'
items.description: The Trump administration has vowed to dismantle the International Criminal Court "brick by brick", but analysts warn it's a move that has more to do with local politics than genuine concerns about the system.

items.title: On farms around Australia, 21st-century slaves are picking our food
items.description: Behind the fruit and vegetables on Australia's supermarket shelves are workers whose stories are rarely heard.

items.title: Household spending increases in June, powered by EV sales
items.description: Australian household spending rose for a second month in June as consumers splashed out on electric vehicles amid rising fuel costs.

items.title: Sydney man charged over fake gun had been at costume party, court told
items.description: A man arrested for carrying a fake gun and wearing a fake police vest at Sydney's Moore Park has been released on bail after a court heard he was attending a costume party.

items.title: Charity cyclist dies one day after completing 5,300km ride
items.description: Motor neurone disease advocate Bob Montgomery dies just one day after completing a 5,300-kilometre bicycle ride across Australia.

items.title: Bystanders deprived Canberra man of 'any chance of survival' after overdose
items.description: A coroner finds a group of bystanders, including two workers from a drug harm minimisation organisation, acted in a "morally blameworthy" manner after waiting hours to call an ambulance for a Canberra man who fatally overdosed.

items.title: In pictures: Garma 2026, a festival for 'everyone'
items.description: The Garma Festival takes place across four days in Gulkula on Gumatj country in a stringybark forest at the top of an escarpment in north-east Arnhem Land.

items.title: Farmer suffered fatal injuries after being headbutted by cow, coroner finds
items.description: A typically safety-conscious farm worker died after being headbutted by a cow while not wearing a helmet, a Tasmanian coroner has ruled.

items.title: No supervision for man who stockpiled chemicals and fantasised about mass killings
items.description: A young man who fantasised about bombing universities and was identified online by the American FBI will be freed into the community with no supervision.

items.title: Solo parenting wasn't for me, so I'm co-parenting with my sister
items.description: Solo parenting, it turns out, wasn't for me. But that's when my sister and I decided to embark on the adventure together.

items.title: From Teardrop to Singapore ban, a guide to Massive Attack
items.description: Massive Attack have landed in Australia for a run of sold-out arena shows this week. If you're wondering what makes them such a big deal, here's your crash course.

items.title: Keen to invest but don't know where to start? Our expert breaks it down
items.description: If you've avoided investing because you've found the terminology intimidating, you're not alone. It can feel like a foreign language when you first start, but it's not as scary as it looks when you get into it.

items.title: New footage shows moment airborne car hit Brisbane bus
items.description: New CCTV footage, captured from inside the bus, shows the moment the car ploughed into it, its front wheels coming to rest on a bus seat.

items.title: Live: ASX nears all-time high
items.description: The Australian share market is now less than a percentage point from a record high. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Sacked for fighting crime, Wendy 'The Enforcer' wins bottle-o job back
items.description: A Tasmanian bottle shop worker who earned the nickname The Enforcer after she used a roller door to deter would-be thieves was sacked by her employer, BWS. But now, Wendy is back in business.

items.title: 'Cocaine dealer' on Mahmood Fazal's Four Corners episode says she did it as 'an acting role'
items.description: Further concerns over the accuracy of reporting by sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal are raised on Media Watch, including that a hire car was used to mislead viewers in the profile of a purported cocaine dealer.

items.title: Ben Carroll names ministry, adds new artificial intelligence portfolio
items.description: The new, slimmed-down Victorian cabinet under Ben Carroll's leadership includes a minister to focus on ethical artificial intelligence, but dumps the transport infrastructure portfolio.

items.title: Older people open to downsizing but facing barriers
items.description: Research shows more than half of people over the age of 55 are open to downsizing. But experts say there are barriers stopping older people moving into smaller homes.

items.title: 'Bohemian' school appoints investigator amid sexual assault allegations
items.description: Six women detail disturbing allegations of abuse and sexualised behaviour from the 1970s through the late 2000s at a controversial alternative school in Melbourne.

items.title: 'Where are the fakers'? NDIS recipient slams argument for overhaul
items.description: NDIS recipient Nicci Carlson, who is in constant pain and may soon lose her eyesight, says cuts to the scheme are making vulnerable people living with a disability scapegoats for Australians hit hard by cost-of-living pressures.
